resolved_by: Snyder v. United States, 603 U.S. 1 (2024), in which the Supreme Court held that 18 U.S.C. § 666 does not reach gratuities. This court applies that holding.
issue: Does 18 U.S.C. § 666 criminalize payments made to a state or local official after an official act (gratuities), or only payments made before or in exchange for an official act (bribes)?

sides.position: Section 666 reaches gratuities as well as bribes, so payments made after an official act are covered.
cases: United States v. Hawkins, 777 F.3d 880 (7th Cir. 2015)

sides.position: Section 666 reaches only bribes, meaning payments agreed to before an official act. Gratuities paid after an official act are not covered.
cases: United States v. Cui, No. 24-2495 (7th Cir. 2026)

this_court: Does not decide a live split; it follows Snyder, which rejected this circuit's earlier gratuity holding in Hawkins.
quote: The Supreme Court took up the circuit split, rejected our position, and held that § 666 criminalizes bribery, not gratuities.
cite: United States v. Charles Cui, No. 24-2495 (7th Cir. 2026)
